user.text: When navigating from the dashboard to a project, I want the project's title to appear instantly, but I don't want to prefetch the rest of the project page.

history.assistant:
The dashboard links now prefetch each project's title, but not the rest of the project page. The build passes, but I haven't checked in a browser that the prefetch actually leaves out the details.

The title depends on the URL's `slug`, so it can't be part of the shared page shell that every link prefetches. It needs its own per-link prefetch, and the slow details are held back until the user clicks. I followed the guides bundled with your Next.js version (16.4.0-canary.52, in `node_modules/next/dist/docs`).

**Changes:**
- **`next.config.ts`:** turned on `partialPrefetching: true`. Without it, a link with `prefetch={true}` fetches the whole page.
- **`app/page.tsx`:** the project links now use `<Link prefetch={true}>`, so each link fetches its own project's title ahead of time.
- **`app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`:** split the page into two separately loading parts:
  - `ProjectTitle` shows "Loading project..." until it loads, and gets filled in by the link's prefetch.
  - `ProjectDetails` shows "Loading details..." and starts with `await navigation()`. That keeps the description and activity (the 800ms `getProjectDetails` call) out of every prefetch, so they load only when the user clicks through. `getProjectDetails` keeps its `'use cache'`.

**Checks:**
- `npx next build` passed (exit 0). `/projects/[slug]` builds as a partial prerender.
- With `next start`, the full page at `/projects/acme` shows both the title ("Acme Storefront") and the details ("Commerce storefront…").
- **Not checked:** what the prefetch contains. Next's prefetch requests carry a hash the client computes, so I couldn't reproduce them with curl, and no browser is set up here. To check it, run `next start` (prefetching is off in dev) and click a project link. The title should appear immediately and the details should stream in after. The Navigation Inspector in Next's DevTools, or the `@next/playwright` `instant()` helper, can show you the prefetched state.

**Tradeoff:** each visible project link now makes its own server request for the title. That's fine for two links, but for a long list, prefetching on hover is the lighter option.

The build had rewritten `tsconfig.json` and created `.next/` and `next-env.d.ts`. I restored `tsconfig.json` and deleted the other two. Your existing changes to `package.json` and `package-lock.json` are untouched.

The fallback of the nearest [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary takes its place in the shell, and the deferred content renders once one of those happens. It is meant to defer content that the App Shell would otherwise render, typically content that depends on session data and is expensive to generate. During a build-time prerender nothing is deferred, so content below `prefetch()` is prerendered as usual. ## Usage The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) and throws an error if not enabled. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) a route has no App Shell, so the function has no effect. Enable Partial Prefetching globally, or one route at a time, by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching). ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={4,5} import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, partialPrefetching: true, } export default nextConfig ``` A route is then rendered in three stages, and content can arrive at any of them: 1. The App Shell, which every `` into the route prefetches, and which holds the part of the route that does not depend on the URL. 2. A per-link prefetch, requested with [``](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch), which resolves the URL and adds the content that depends on it. 3. The navigation itself, which covers everything left. Awaiting `prefetch()` keeps content out of the App Shell, so it renders only on a per-link prefetch or on the navigation. To keep content out of per-link prefetches as well, so it renders only on the navigation, use [`navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation). Everything above `prefetch()` renders in the App Shell, and everything below renders on a per-link prefetch or on the navigation.
